Gamepad driver missing — nothing will move yet

The ViGEmBus driver is not installed, so this app cannot create a virtual controller. Your phone will still connect and look like it is working, but every button press is ignored until the driver is installed.

Install it from github.com/ViGEm/ViGEmBus/releases, then restart this app.

  1. Open the address above on your phone, on the same Wi-Fi as this PC.
  2. Click your game's window on this PC so it has the keyboard focus.
  3. Press something on the phone — the Live input panel below should light up.

Blocked by Windows Firewall? If Windows asked for permission when this app started, it must be allowed on private networks. Without that, your phone cannot reach this PC at all. You can change it later under Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → Allow an app through firewall.

Windows' “Game Controllers” (joy.cpl) test page will show this pad in its list but will not show its buttons or axes moving. That page reads the old DirectInput API, which Xbox-type controllers — real ones included — don't report through. It's expected, and nothing is wrong. This monitor and your games both read the same XInput state the pad actually publishes.
